1.reason: follow-up: the row's age is measured from queued_at and includes upstream waits; either label it as queued age or measure admissible age per request

findings.text: non-blocking: _stall_verdicts already reads the admission verdict log into a latest-verdict-per-run mapping and filters on queue_admission.STALL_VERDICT, which is exactly what admission_verdicts at reckon/crew/obligations.py:700 re-implements; the owner is unreachable from production (no module imports needs_you since the follower pane dropped its last caller), so the duplicate will drift from the copy the six needs_you test files still exercise, and the natural owner for both is the module that defines the log and its verdict words, reckon/crew/queue_admission.py.

non-blocking: the docstring says the forwarded age "is how long the request has been admissible, not how long it has existed ... and only the pass measures the difference", but the field read one line later from the verdict row is set by queue_admission._record_stalls (reckon/crew/queue_admission.py:1487) as moment minus queued_at, which includes any wait on upstream refs since only the plan-review hold release shifts queued_at; the pass-level admissible_age_seconds is a different, aggregate field, so a request released from awaiting-upstream after an hour reports an hour, and the landing fragment repeats the same claim.

non-blocking: the stall fixture writes the same constant into the pass-level admissible_age_seconds (:66) and the per-row age_seconds (:73), so the age assertions at :120 and :138 hold whichever of the two fields the row reads; distinct values would make those assertions discriminate, which matters because the docstring's claim about admissibility turns on exactly that difference.
